Photo 2 shows a close-up of the gearbox/transmission housing lying on dirty pavement, with a person's feet and jeans visible for scale, plus the same wiring harness mess.
All three photos show heavy dirt, grime, and debris (what looks like wood shavings or packing material) stuck to the housings.
A watermark reading 'GEARUP INC.' is visible across all photos, suggesting these are stock/listing photos from a parts dealer, not necessarily unique to this specific unit.
No visible VIN plate, part number tag, or identification sticker legible on the gearbox casing in any photo.
Items sit outdoors directly on bare asphalt/ground, no indoor or climate-controlled storage visible.
The assembly includes a full engine (visible valve covers, intake, injectors) attached to the transmission, not just a standalone gearbox as the text claims.
Seller's new message is text only, reasserting prior claims; no new photo or video was provided.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened
claims.evidence: No test video, dipstick/fluid check, or bench-test clip provided; a static photo cannot confirm function, mileage, or internal condition.

claims.claim: 'I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true' (seller's verbal reassurance)
claims.evidence: A verbal claim with no accompanying photo or video is not independent evidence; it is the same unverified claim restated.

risks.risk: Internal transmission condition (gears, synchros, seals, torque converter if automatic) cannot be assessed from exterior photos.
risks.proof: A video of the gearbox being turned by hand or bench-tested, plus a shot of the fluid on a dipstick/pan for color and metal shavings.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / needing rebuild

risks.risk: Claim says 'gearbox' but photos show a full engine attached, raising doubt about what is actually being sold and whether the price is for the gearbox alone or the full assembly.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the gearbox separated from the engine, or a close-up of the bolted bell-housing interface confirming it can be detached.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the cheaper standalone gearbox, not as an engine+transmission combo

risks.risk: Heavy dirt and debris could be concealing cracks, weld repairs, or corrosion on the casing.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the casing after wiping down the dirt, especially around mounting points and the bell housing.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetically rough/unknown structural integrity

risks.risk: No model/part tag visible, so exact fitment to E150 vs E250 vs E350 (different GVWR, possibly different transmission ratios) cannot be confirmed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped part number or tag on the transmission case.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/unconfirmed fitment, buyer assumes compatibility risk

risks.risk: Outdoor storage on bare ground raises risk of moisture ingress into seals/electronics (if automatic with solenoids).
risks.proof: Photo/video showing the transmission pan and any electrical connectors free of rust or water staining.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possible moisture damage, not confirmed functional

proof_requests: Video of the gearbox being rotated or bench-tested to support 'tested and working' claim.
Close-up photo of any stamped part/casting number on the transmission housing.
Photo showing the gearbox clearly separated from the engine, since the listing says 'gearbox' but photos show a full engine attached.
Photo of transmission fluid condition (color, debris) via dipstick or drain plug.
Any import/customs documentation to support 'direct from Belgium' claim.
response.reason: The seller's spoken reassurance adds no new visual evidence; the listing still claims a standalone tested gearbox while photos show an unlabelled, dirt-covered engine-and-transmission assembly, so fitment and function remain unconfirmed.
